questions.title: Secretions of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei
questions.question: The supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei secrete all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Oxytocin is one of the two hormones synthesised by the magnocellular neurons of these nuclei, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) is the second hormone made by these nuclei and transported to the pars nervosa, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. The magnocellular neurons of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesise only oxytocin and vasopressin, which pass down the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract to be stored in Herring bodies of the pars nervosa. Beta-endorphin is an opioid peptide cleaved from pro-opiomelanocortin in anterior-pituitary corticotrophs and arcuate neurons, not a product of these magnocellular nuclei, so it is the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Because endorphin is genuinely not a product of these nuclei, there is a valid exception, so 'none of the above' cannot be selected.

questions.learning_objective: List the hormones of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei and identify endorphin as the odd one out.

questions.title: Nature of pituicytes
questions.question: Pituicytes:

options.A: Are found in the pars distalis
options.B: Are a type of glial cell

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pituicytes are confined to the pars nervosa (posterior lobe); they are not found in the pars distalis.
explanations.B: Correct. Pituicytes are branched glial cells, related to astrocytes, and are the only resident cell of the pars nervosa. They give structural and metabolic support to the unmyelinated hypothalamic axons that store and release the posterior-pituitary hormones, but they do not secrete hormone themselves.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vasopressin is synthesised by hypothalamic magnocellular neurons and only stored in the pars nervosa; pituicytes do not produce it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Prolactin is a product of the acidophil mammotrophs of the pars distalis, not of pituicytes.

questions.learning_objective: Identify pituicytes as the glial support cells of the pars nervosa.

questions.title: Contents of the pars nervosa
questions.question: The pars nervosa contains all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct. The pars nervosa is made of the unmyelinated axons of hypothalamic magnocellular neurons, their Herring-body storage terminals, glial pituicytes and fenestrated capillaries. The neuron cell bodies lie in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus, so the pars nervosa itself contains no nerve cell bodies, making this the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pituicytes are the resident glial cells of the pars nervosa, so they are present.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Herring bodies are the dilated axon terminals that store oxytocin and vasopressin in the pars nervosa, so they are present.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pars nervosa is supplied by fenestrated capillaries that receive the released hormones, so they are present.

questions.learning_objective: State that the pars nervosa holds axons, Herring bodies and pituicytes but not neuron cell bodies.

questions.title: Orange G staining specificity
questions.question: Orange G specifically stains:

explanations.A: Correct. Orange G is an acid dye taken up by the acidophils of the pars distalis (somatotrophs and mammotrophs), which appear orange. Orange-G positivity is therefore a selective marker of the acidophil population.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Basophils are instead PAS-positive because of the carbohydrate of their glycoprotein hormones; they are not stained by orange G.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Chromophobes are poorly granulated cells with little staining affinity and do not take up orange G.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pituicytes are glial cells of the pars nervosa and are not stained by orange G.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise orange G as a selective stain for pars distalis acidophils.

questions.title: Staining and size of pituitary basophils
questions.question: Regarding basophils of the pars distalis:

options.A: Are larger than acidophils in size
options.B: Are more than acidophils in number

explanations.A: Incorrect as a sole answer. Basophils are indeed larger than acidophils, but this is only part of the correct combination.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Basophils are not more numerous than acidophils; acidophils typically outnumber them, so any option relying on this statement is wrong.
explanations.C: Incorrect as a sole answer. Basophils do stain strongly with PAS because their glycoprotein-hormone granules carry carbohydrate, but this is only part of the correct combination.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This pairs the true 'larger than acidophils' with the false 'more than acidophils in number', so it is wrong.
explanations.E: Correct. Basophils of the pars distalis are larger than the acidophils and their glycoprotein-hormone granules are PAS-positive. Both statements A and C are true, so the combined choice is the single best answer, whereas statement B (greater number) is false.

questions.learning_objective: Contrast basophils (larger, PAS-positive) with acidophils (smaller, orange-G-positive).

questions.title: Hormones of the chromophils
questions.question: All of the following hormones are secreted by chromophils EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. ACTH is secreted by basophil corticotrophs, which are chromophils of the pars distalis, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. TSH is a glycoprotein hormone of the basophil thyrotrophs, which are chromophils, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Correct. Chromophils are the granulated, hormone-secreting cells of the pars distalis (acidophils and basophils). Oxytocin is not an anterior-pituitary product: it is synthesised by hypothalamic paraventricular and supraoptic neurons and merely stored in the pars nervosa, so it is the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. FSH is a glycoprotein hormone of the basophil gonadotrophs, which are chromophils, so it is not the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Separate anterior-pituitary chromophil hormones from the neurohypophyseal hormone oxytocin.

questions.title: Secretion of the pars intermedia
questions.question: In reptiles, the pars intermedia secretes:

explanations.A: Incorrect. ACTH is a product of the basophil corticotrophs of the pars distalis, not of the pars intermedia.
explanations.B: Incorrect. TSH is secreted by the thyrotrophs of the pars distalis, not by the pars intermedia.
explanations.C: Correct. The pars intermedia contains basophilic cells that cleave pro-opiomelanocortin to melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH), which acts on melanocytes to increase melanin synthesis. In lower vertebrates such as reptiles and amphibians this drives adaptive skin-colour change; in humans the pars intermedia is rudimentary.
explanations.D: Incorrect. FSH is a gonadotroph product of the pars distalis, not of the pars intermedia.

questions.learning_objective: Identify MSH as the secretory product of the pars intermedia.

questions.title: Role of lysosomes in thyroid follicular cells
questions.question: In follicular cells of the thyroid gland, lysosomes are essential because their enzymes carry out:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Thyroglobulin is synthesised on the rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus, not by lysosomes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Iodination of thyroglobulin occurs extracellularly at the apical membrane in the follicular lumen (colloid), catalysed by thyroid peroxidase, not by lysosomal enzymes.
explanations.C: Correct. To release hormone, follicular cells endocytose iodinated thyroglobulin from the colloid, and the colloid droplets fuse with lysosomes whose proteolytic enzymes hydrolyse thyroglobulin. This proteolysis liberates free T3 and T4, which then diffuse into the blood, so lysosomes are essential for hormone release.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Iodide trapping is performed by the basal sodium-iodide symporter of the follicular cell membrane, not by lysosomes.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that follicular-cell lysosomes hydrolyse thyroglobulin to release T3 and T4.

questions.title: Features of parathyroid oxyphil cells
questions.question: Oxyphil cells of the parathyroid gland are characterised by the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Few in number and large in size

explanations.A: Incorrect. Oxyphil cells are indeed few in number and larger than the chief cells, so this is a true feature, not the exception.
explanations.B: Correct. Oxyphil cells have a cytoplasm packed with mitochondria, which makes them strongly acidophilic (eosinophilic), not basophilic. Describing them as strongly basophilic is therefore the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Oxyphils are generally regarded as degenerated or inactive chief cells, so this is a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Oxyphil cells appear around puberty and increase in number with age, so this is a true feature.

questions.learning_objective: Describe parathyroid oxyphil cells as large, few, acidophilic and age-related.

questions.title: Cells of the adrenal medulla
questions.question: The cells of the adrenal medulla are:

explanations.A: Incorrect as a sole answer. Chromaffin cells are the principal cells, but they are not the only neural cells present in the medulla.
explanations.B: Incorrect as a sole answer. Sympathetic ganglion cells are present but scattered; they are not the whole cellular composition.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The adrenal medulla is a modified sympathetic ganglion and does not consist of glial cells.
explanations.D: Correct. The adrenal medulla is a modified sympathetic ganglion, so its principal cells are the chromaffin cells, modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons that store catecholamines and give the chromaffin reaction. Scattered among them are true sympathetic ganglion cells. Both populations are therefore present, which makes the combined choice the single best answer.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the two neural cell populations of the adrenal medulla.

questions.title: Regulation and nature of mineralocorticoids
questions.question: Mineralocorticoids are:

explanations.A: Correct. Mineralocorticoids, chiefly aldosterone, are steroid hormones made in the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex. Their secretion is controlled mainly by the renin-angiotensin system, in which angiotensin II stimulates the glomerulosa to release aldosterone. A rise in plasma potassium acts as a second stimulus, whereas ACTH plays only a minor permissive role here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mineralocorticoids are secreted from the zona glomerulosa; the zona fasciculata secretes glucocorticoids.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Regulation of carbohydrate metabolism is a glucocorticoid (cortisol) action; mineralocorticoids regulate sodium, potassium and water balance.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mineralocorticoids are steroid hormones derived from cholesterol, not proteins.

questions.learning_objective: State that angiotensin II is the main regulator of mineralocorticoid secretion.

questions.title: Composition of paraganglia
questions.question: Paraganglia are aggregates of:

explanations.A: Correct. Paraganglia are small collections of chromaffin cells located outside the adrenal medulla, alongside the sympathetic chain and autonomic plexuses. A well-known example is the para-aortic bodies of Zuckerkandl. Like the medullary cells they are neural-crest-derived and store catecholamines, which is why they are chromaffin rather than cortical aggregates.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Zona reticularis cells are steroid-secreting cortical cells, not the chromaffin cells that form paraganglia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Zona fasciculata cells are cortical glucocorticoid-secreting cells, not chromaffin cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Zona glomerulosa cells are cortical mineralocorticoid-secreting cells, not chromaffin cells.

questions.learning_objective: Define paraganglia as extra-adrenal aggregates of chromaffin cells.

questions.title: Secretions of pinealocytes
questions.question: Regarding pinealocytes:

explanations.A: Incorrect as a sole answer. Pinealocytes do secrete melatonin at night, but this is only part of the correct combination.
explanations.B: Incorrect as a sole answer. Pinealocytes do secrete serotonin during daylight, but this is only part of the correct combination.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The supporting interstitial (glial) cells of the pineal resemble astrocytes; the pinealocytes themselves are the neuroendocrine secretory cells, so this statement does not describe pinealocytes.
explanations.D: Correct. Pinealocyte secretion follows the light-dark cycle. Melatonin is released during darkness at night, while its precursor serotonin predominates during daylight. Both statements A and B are therefore true, which makes the combined choice the single best answer.
explanations.E: Incorrect. This pairs the true melatonin statement with the false 'resemble astrocytes' statement, so it is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: State that pinealocytes secrete melatonin at night and serotonin by day.

questions.title: Brain sand of the pineal gland
questions.question: Brain sand (corpora arenacea) of the pineal gland:

options.A: Is found only in the diseased pineal body
options.B: Serves as a landmark for radiologists

explanations.A: Incorrect. Corpora arenacea are a normal, age-related accumulation of calcified concretions, not a marker of pineal disease.
explanations.B: Correct. Corpora arenacea are calcified, radio-opaque concretions that accumulate in the midline pineal gland. Because they show up on skull radiographs and CT, they serve as a useful landmark. A shift of this calcified pineal from the midline signals a space-occupying lesion, which is the classic clinical use.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Corpora arenacea are calcified (mineralised) concretions that stain with haematoxylin (basophilic), not intensely acidophilic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Brain sand accumulates and increases with age rather than decreasing throughout life.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise corpora arenacea as calcified pineal bodies used as a midline radiological landmark.
